{{Short description|Iranian biologist}}
'''Samuel Rahbar''' ({{langx|fa|سموئیلِ رهبر}} ''Samu'il-e Rahbar'' May 12, 1929 - November 10, 2012) was an Iranian scientist who discovered <ref name="pmid5808299">{{cite journal |author1=Rahbar S |author2=Blumenfeld O |author3=Ranney HM |title=Studies of an unusual hemoglobin in patients with diabetes mellitus |journal=Biochem. Biophys. Res. Commun. |volume=36 |issue=5 |pages=838–43 |year=1969 |pmid=5808299 |doi=10.1016/0006-291X(69)90685-8}}</ref> the linkage between diabetes and [[HbA1C]], a form of [[hemoglobin]] used primarily to identify [[blood plasma|plasma]] [[glucose]] [[concentration]] over time.

Rahbar was born into a Jewish family in the Iranian city of [[Hamedan]] in 1929. He obtained his [[Doctor of Medicine|MD]] degree from the [[University of Tehran]] in 1953 and a [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] degree in [[immunology]] from the same university in 1963.

From 1952 to 1960 Rahbar pursued mainly clinical activities in [[Abadan]] and [[Tehran]], returning to academic life as a postdoctoral fellow in 1959. After earning his PhD, he was promoted to [[assistant professor]] in 1963 and to [[associate professor]] in 1965 in the Department of Immunology.

Rahbar spent 1968–1969 as a visiting scientist at the Department of Medicine of the [[Albert Einstein College of Medicine]] in New York, where he collaborated with [[List of Barnard College people|Helen M. Ranney]]. After his return to Tehran, Rahbar was promoted to [[full professor]] in 1970 and to director of the Department of Applied Biology in the University of Tehran Medical School in Tehran. 
 
After the Islamic Revolution in Iran, Rahbar was laid off from his position as Director  of the Department of Applied Biology at Tehran University. As a result of this unfair treatment he decided to take his family and leave the country in 1979.

1979 Rahbar became a researcher and professor of diabetes in the Department of Diabetes, Endocrinology, and Metabolism at the [[City of Hope Medical Center|City of Hope]] in [[Duarte, California|Duarte]], [[California]] (in [[Los Angeles County]]).<ref name="ADA Award1">{{Cite web|url=http://www.cityofhope.org/about/publications/hope-news/2012-vol-07-num-14-june-4/Pages/samuel-rahbar-will-receive-national-scientific-and-health-care-achievement-award-for-diabetes-work.aspx|title = City of Hope}}</ref>

In 2012, the [[American Diabetes Association]] (ADA) bestowed a special, one-time National Scientific Achievement Award on Rahbar in recognition of his discovery of HbA1c as a marker of glycemic status in persons with diabetes.  The award is named after the awardee and is called the Samuel Rahbar Outstanding Discovery Award.<ref name="ADA Award2">{{cite web |url=http://www.diabetes.org/about-us/national-achievement-awards-2012/national-science-and-health/rahbar-outstanding-discovery-2012.html |title=Samuel Rahbar Outstanding Discovery Award - American Diabetes Association |accessdate=2012-06-06 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://archive.today/20130414171216/http://www.diabetes.org/about-us/national-achievement-awards-2012/national-science-and-health/rahbar-outstanding-discovery-2012.html |archivedate=2013-04-14 }}</ref>
